h1: Point of sale material for beer in Indian wine shops and supermarkets
title: Beer Point of Sale Material in India | Craft Beer School
desc: What point of sale material works for craft beer in Indian wine shops and supermarkets, what the rules allow and how to keep it out of the storeroom.
teaser: Most shelf talkers sent to Indian liquor stores never leave the box. Here is how to make ones that do.
standfirst: Point of sale material is the cheapest advertising a craft brewery can buy in India and also the most wasted. Here is what earns its place on a crowded shelf and what the regulations allow.
sections: Why point of sale matters more in India

Direct advertising of alcohol is restricted in India, so the store is one of the few places a brewery can speak to a buyer at the moment of choice. A shopper in a wine shop is already buying. The question is whether they reach for the mass-market lager they always buy or try something new. A good shelf strip or fridge sticker can tip that choice.

The catch: rules on branding inside and outside licensed premises vary by state. Some states are strict about signage, display and anything that looks like advertising. Before you print, check what your state and the store's licence allow. Our guide to alcohol advertising rules in India explains the general picture. The specifics need a licensing consultant.
Know the two kinds of store

Wine shops and standalone liquor stores are usually small, crowded and staffed by people who hand bottles over a counter. Space is scarce and the owner decides what goes up. Material must be small, durable and useful to the staff, not only to shoppers.

Supermarkets and premium stores with liquor sections in states that allow them have open chillers, aisles and planograms agreed at head-office level. Material goes through a category manager and must fit their fixtures. Here, a tidy shelf strip and a well-designed carton matter more than a poster.

Our guide to on-trade and off-trade covers how these channels differ for a brewery's sales plan.

• Shelf strips and wobblers. Small, cheap and they sit exactly where the beer is. Print the beer name, style and one line on taste.
  • Fridge door stickers. If the owner allows them, a sticker at eye level on the right door tells shoppers where to look. Use durable vinyl that survives condensation and cleaning.
  • Style guides for staff. A laminated card behind the counter that explains each beer in one line. Counter staff are asked "what is this?" all day. Give them an answer.
  • Branded carton faces. Outer cartons stacked on the floor are point of sale too, so print them like it.

Large posters, standees and elaborate display units often go straight to a back room. Owners have no wall space, staff move them to restock and many end up with the flex banners from the last big-brand promotion. Price boards and anything that suggests a discount may also run into state rules on pricing and promotion.

Before you print a thousand of anything, ask five store owners what they would actually put up. They will tell you.
Design for heat, hands and cleaning

Indian liquor stores are hard on paper. Fridges sweat, staff wipe surfaces and the summer sun through the shopfront fades inks within weeks. Choose laminated or synthetic stock, UV-resistant inks for anything near a window and adhesives that come off cleanly, because owners hate residue on their fridge glass and will refuse your next sticker if this one left a mess.

Keep the design consistent with your cans. A shopper should connect the strip to the pack instantly: same colour, same type, same beer name. Point of sale that looks like a different brand helps nobody.
Make it part of the sales visit

Point of sale only works if someone puts it up and replaces it. Give each salesperson a small kit: strips, stickers, the staff card and a roll of tape. On every visit they check the beer is in the fridge, faced forward and labelled. They photograph it. Over a month, those photos tell you which stores keep your material up and which do not.

This routine also builds goodwill with the owner, which in Indian liquor retail often matters more than the material itself. A store that likes your rep will move your beer to the fridge.

1. Confirm what your state and the store licence allow.
  2. Ask owners what they would use.
  3. Print small, durable pieces in your pack colours.
  4. Put them in a kit with every sales visit.
  5. Photograph, track and reprint what works.

Matching point of sale to the pack, the shelf and the rules is a packaging job as much as a sales one, which is why we teach it alongside label and can design.
faqs: Is point of sale material for beer legal in India?
It depends on the state and the store's licence. Some states restrict signage and display in or near liquor stores, so check with a licensing consultant before you print.
What is the cheapest point of sale that works?
Shelf strips and a laminated staff card explaining each beer. They are small, useful and stay where the beer is.
Should I offer discounts on shelf material?
Be careful. Pricing and promotion rules for alcohol vary by state. Many store owners dislike price messaging they did not set. Focus on what the beer tastes like.
